Definition: something bought, i.e. property, but only livestock; abstractly, acquisition
BiblicalUsage: The word is cattle, livestock, the property that walks. The hand of the LORD falls on the cattle of Egypt in the field, and all the cattle of Egypt die of the murrain, while Job's wealth is counted in sheep and camels and oxen before the day it is all taken away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe cattle are the measure of wealth in the old world, and the measure shows how quickly wealth goes: the same word that counts Job's thousands counts their loss.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
